title: BUILD TOTAL
subtitle: 8-Week Powerlifting Performance Programme
description: A focused eight-week powerlifting build-and-peak programme using competition-lift practice, targeted volume, submaximal singles, autoregulation, a mid-block pivot and a competition or testing taper.
intended_athlete: Adults with at least six months of consistent barbell training who can already squat, bench press and deadlift safely and train four core days per week.
not_for: Complete beginners who need to learn the three lifts
Athletes seeking an unsupervised rapid weight cut
Athletes unable to recover from four lifting days
entry_gate: Has at least six months of consistent barbell training and can perform the squat, bench press and deadlift with repeatable technique.
Can complete four lifting sessions per week, normally 60-90 minutes, and protect at least two non-lifting days.
Has a trustworthy recent competition-standard 1RM or technically clean 2-5 repetition set for each lift.
Can train with safeties and/or competent spotters and has access to a barbell, plates, rack and bench.
Is not relying on this programme to diagnose pain, rehabilitate injury or teach unfamiliar maximal lifting without in-person coaching.

readiness_options.label: Green - ready
readiness_options.action: Complete the prescription. The stated RPE cap still applies.

readiness_options.label: Amber - under-recovered
readiness_options.action: Remove the top single or cap it at RPE 6, reduce back-off load 5%, remove one work set and omit the final accessory.

readiness_options.label: Red - materially fatigued or unwell
readiness_options.action: Use 2-3 technique sets at 50-60% only or end the session. Do not move heavy work to the next day.

readiness_options.label: Pain changes movement
readiness_options.action: Stop the painful lift. Do not test it with more load; use a pain-free option only with appropriate guidance or seek assessment.

foundation.title: What eight weeks can honestly do
foundation.summary: Eight weeks can organise and express existing capacity; it cannot replace years of technical practice and muscle development.
points: Build useful submaximal volume before reducing repetitions and raising specificity.
Practise the competition lifts frequently enough to improve skill without maxing them constantly.
Use top singles to rehearse heavy technique and calibrate readiness, not to prove strength every week.
Reduce fatigue in Week 4, intensify in Weeks 5-6 and taper in Weeks 7-8.
Finish with a competition, controlled gym test or training peak according to the athlete profile.
foundation.coach_rule: A programme can reveal strength only when it first creates training the athlete can recover from.

foundation.title: The weekly structure
foundation.summary: Four core lifting days spread specific practice and muscle-building work across the week.
points: Monday: competition squat priority plus competition bench volume.
Tuesday: competition bench priority plus deadlift variation or volume.
Thursday: squat secondary work plus bench variation or specific volume.
Saturday: competition deadlift priority plus light bench technique.
Sunday: optional easy recovery and a lesson; it never replaces a core lifting day.
foundation.coach_rule: Move days when necessary, but preserve the order and avoid compressing all four sessions into consecutive days.

foundation.title: How to use every prescription
foundation.summary: Percentages organise the plan; RPE caps protect it from day-to-day variation and false precision.
points: Calculate percentages from the reference max recorded before Week 1.
Round working loads down to the nearest available increment when the exact number is unavailable.
A top single is one technically clean repetition at the stated RPE - never a hidden max attempt.
Back-off work stops when the RPE cap, movement standard or prescribed repetitions can no longer be met.
Log the actual load, repetitions, RPE, standards and any change; never auto-fill the published prescription as completed.
foundation.coach_rule: When percentage and RPE disagree, use the lighter load that preserves the prescribed effort and technique.

foundation.title: The programme is not an injury test
foundation.summary: Powerlifting training can be performed safely, but high load does not make pain irrelevant.
points: Use correctly positioned safeties and competent spotters for squat and bench press.
Do not grind through pain that changes bar path, range, stance, grip or bracing.
Do not repeat failed repetitions in normal training.
Stop for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, sudden neurological symptoms or another concerning acute symptom and seek urgent medical help.
Return after injury, illness, pregnancy or a medical issue with appropriate professional guidance.
foundation.coach_rule: The app cannot see the lift, inspect equipment or assess symptoms. Text and timers do not replace competent coaching or healthcare.

competition_standards.scope: These summaries follow the IPF technical rulebook effective 1 March 2026. Other federations may differ. Always verify the current rules for the athlete event.

squat.standard: Begin motionless and erect with knees locked. Descend until the top of the legs at the hip joint is lower than the top of the knees. Return to an upright, knees-locked finish and wait for Rack.
common_failures: Unlocking or moving before the command
Feet stepping or moving laterally before Rack
Failing to finish erect with knees locked

bench_press.standard: Begin with elbows locked and the body in the required position. Lower the bar to the chest or abdominal area and the underside of both elbow joints to at least level with or below the top of each shoulder joint, hold it motionless, press to locked elbows and wait for Rack.
common_failures: Head, shoulders or buttocks losing required contact
Feet lifting or no longer remaining flat
Downward movement of the whole bar

deadlift.standard: Lift the bar until standing erect with knees locked and the front of the shoulders behind the imaginary projection of the bar. Hold the bar motionless until Down, then return it under control with both hands.
common_failures: Supporting the bar on the thighs

competition_standards.attempts: Three attempts are allowed on each lift; the best valid squat, bench press and deadlift form the total. Normal IPF attempts use 2.5 kg increments, with specific exceptions for records.

primary: 20 kg or 15 kg barbell as appropriate
Basic leg and hamstring accessory equipment
competition_specific: Singlet and legal clothing for the chosen federation
equipment.principle: Use the safest stable variation that preserves the intended muscle or movement function. Competition practice should use the athlete competition setup whenever practical.

variation_library.rule: Choose one for Weeks 1-4 and do not rotate weekly.
Keep shoulder and wrist positions tolerable; use safeties.

variation_library.default: Two-count pause deadlift below the knee
variation_library.rule: Use a lighter load and stop if the variation changes the competition stance or grip unintentionally.

variation_library.default: Bulgarian split squat or leg press
variation_library.rule: Select a stable pain-free option and progress repetitions before load.
Avoid turning the movement into lumbar fatigue before deadlifting.
Use controlled repetitions and avoid failure soreness that alters the next squat or deadlift.

attempt_planner.scope: Coaching heuristics, not federation rules or guaranteed percentages. The final choice responds to recent legal singles, readiness and coach judgement.

opener.starting_band: Often about 88-92% of a current defensible max
opener.rule: A weight already demonstrated to full standard and available on a poor day.

second.starting_band: Often about 94-98% of a current defensible max
second.rule: Secure a strong total. Adjust from opener speed and standard.

third.effort: RPE 9-10 only when testing is appropriate
third.rule: Choose after the second. A small valid personal best beats an invented target and a miss.

attempt_planner.failed_attempt_rule: Do not automatically add load after a miss. Repeat or reduce unless a competent coach identifies a clear correctable reason and the next attempt remains safe.

tests: Weekly competition-lift top single load/RPE where prescribed
Week 8 valid squat, bench press, deadlift and total or RPE-8 training peak
progress.completion_rule: Four core sessions is a full week. Optional recovery and education are tracked separately.
progress.success_definition: A stronger or more technically reliable valid total, better submaximal execution, or a clearer next-block decision. No increase is guaranteed in eight weeks.

learn.title: Powerlifting is skill-specific strength
learn.summary: The sport rewards the heaviest valid squat, bench press and deadlift, so muscle, force production and competition execution all matter.
points: Specific practice improves the exact task tested.
Hypertrophy and accessories support future force production but do not replace the competition lifts.
Technical consistency matters more as load rises.
A valid total is three successful best lifts, not the sum of gym rumours.

learn.title: Reference max, percentage and rounding
learn.summary: A reference max is a current, defensible planning number - not an all-time lift from a different bodyweight or standard.
points: Use a recent valid single or a clean 2-5 rep set.
For a 2-5 rep set, the app may estimate 1RM with Epley and must label it an estimate.
Do not increase the reference max during the block because one day felt easy.
Round loads down when plates cannot create the exact percentage.
The RPE cap overrides the percentage on a poor day.

learn.title: RPE and repetitions in reserve
learn.summary: RPE estimates how many technically acceptable repetitions remain; it improves with practice and is less accurate far from failure.
points: RPE 10 means no repetition remains; RPE 9 roughly one; RPE 8 roughly two.
Rate the set immediately after racking or lowering the bar.
Use bar speed, position and prior experience together.
Do not call a slow technical breakdown RPE 8 because the bar eventually moved.
The plan never requires perfect RPE accuracy; it requires honest conservative decisions.

reference.programme_use: Only a final test attempt when appropriate.

learn.title: Why the plan uses volume, frequency and specificity
learn.summary: More training can produce more adaptation, but returns diminish and recoverability differs between athletes and lifts.
points: Bench press is practised frequently because each exposure can remain small and technically focused.
Squat and deadlift volume is spread across competition and secondary exposures.
Sets fall as intensity and competition specificity rise.
The dose is a starting prescription, not proof that every athlete needs the same volume.
Persistent performance decline means the athlete needs less stress, not more motivation copy.

learn.title: Top singles are practice, not weekly tests
learn.summary: A submaximal single rehearses setup, bracing, commands and confidence with low repetition fatigue.
points: Warm up with the fewest jumps that create readiness.
Stop the single at the prescribed RPE even if a heavier lift appears available.
A miss ends heavy loading for that lift that day.
The Week 6 ceiling is RPE 8.5, not a disguised max.
The Week 7 single should look like an opener: confident, legal and repeatable.

learn.title: Squat execution and standards
learn.summary: Begin motionless and erect with knees locked. Descend until the top of the legs at the hip joint is lower than the top of the knees. Return to an upright, knees-locked finish and wait for Rack.
points: Set rack and safety heights before loading.
Brace before the walkout and use the fewest stable steps.
Train the depth that must pass, not the depth that only looks close from one angle.
Keep the bar over a stable mid-foot path appropriate to the athlete style.
Practise Squat and Rack commands during selected singles.

learn.title: Bench press execution and standards
learn.summary: Begin with elbows locked and the body in the required position. Lower the bar to the chest or abdominal area and the underside of both elbow joints to at least level with or below the top of each shoulder joint, hold it motionless, press to locked elbows and wait for Rack.
points: Use safeties and a competent handoff when available.
Set grip, upper back and feet before unracking.
Practise the current elbow-depth requirement and a motionless pause.
Press without losing required body contact or foot position.
Use Start, Press and Rack commands during selected singles.

learn.title: Deadlift execution and standards
learn.summary: Lift the bar until standing erect with knees locked and the front of the shoulders behind the imaginary projection of the bar. Hold the bar motionless until Down, then return it under control with both hands.
points: Choose conventional or sumo before the block and avoid changing without a coaching reason.
Create tension before breaking the floor.
Keep the bar close without supporting it on the thighs.
Finish knees and hips together, then wait for Down.
Return the bar under control with both hands.

learn.title: Accessories build capacity; they do not win recovery battles
learn.summary: Accessories target muscle and positions that support the three lifts while keeping fatigue proportionate.
points: Most accessory sets finish with 2-3 good repetitions available.
Choose stable movements that can be progressed and logged.
Remove accessories before removing important competition-lift work on an Amber day.
Accessories reduce sharply after Week 6 and disappear during the final taper.
Do not turn assistance work into unlogged conditioning.

learn.title: Rest, recovery and readiness
learn.summary: Hard sets need enough rest to reproduce force; weeks need enough recovery to express adaptation.
points: Rest 3-5 minutes for main work and longer when a heavy single genuinely requires it.
Use 90-180 seconds for accessories according to performance.
Protect an individualised sleep opportunity and routine.
Do not catch up missed heavy sessions by doubling the next day.
Use readiness to modify the dose, not to manufacture an excuse for testing.

learn.title: Food, protein and bodyweight
learn.summary: Strength training requires sufficient energy, protein, carbohydrate and fluid; aggressive weight manipulation can compete with performance.
points: A protein intake around 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day is sufficient for most exercising adults according to the cited ISSN position stand.
Use carbohydrate around demanding training according to preference and tolerance.
Keep normal hydration and practise meet-day food before Week 8.
Do not begin an acute weight cut from a generic app instruction.
For a short weigh-in, choose a class that can be reached without dangerous improvisation and use qualified sports-dietetic support for any manipulation.

learn.title: Pain, injury and pelvic-health awareness
learn.summary: Powerlifting injury incidence appears relatively low per training hour, but painful conditions that affect training are common and evidence does not identify one simple cause.
points: Pain that changes movement ends the lift for that day.
Avoid diagnosing an injury from the exercise name or a social-media checklist.
Seek appropriate assessment for persistent, worsening or neurological symptoms.
Female and male lifters can experience pelvic-floor symptoms; leaking is common enough to discuss but should not be dismissed as inevitable.
Technique and load management matter, but no programme can promise injury prevention.

learn.title: Why and how the taper works
learn.summary: The taper reduces fatigue faster than fitness disappears, but the exact best taper remains individual and powerlifting-specific evidence is limited.
points: Training volume falls substantially across Weeks 7-8.
Heavy technique remains briefly through opener rehearsal.
Deadlift work finishes earlier because many lifters experience greater recovery cost, but this remains individual.
Accessories disappear before the test.
Do not add missed volume, novel conditioning or hard failure work because the taper feels easy.

learn.title: Attempt selection and meet-day decisions
learn.summary: The opener establishes the total, the second builds it and the third responds to the day.
points: Choose an opener already demonstrated to competition standard and available on a poor day.
Use the second to secure a strong total before chasing a speculative third.
Select the third from the speed, standard and RPE of the second attempt.
A failed attempt is normally repeated or increased only with a clear technical reason and coach judgement.
At IPF competition, second and third attempts must be submitted within one minute; rules on changes vary by attempt and lift.

learn.title: After Week 8
learn.summary: A peak is followed by recovery and review, not an immediate second peak.
points: Take several days away from heavy lifting after a maximal test or competition.
Review successful lifts, failed standards, readiness, pain and bodyweight context.
Update reference maxes only from valid results.
Choose one technical and one physical priority for the next block.
Return to accumulation before another peak unless the next event demands a carefully coached exception.

blocks.name: General and specific warm-up
blocks.instruction: 5-8 minutes easy movement, then 2-4 mobility or activation drills that improve today's competition squat. Build through empty-bar and progressively heavier sets using low repetitions. Warm up; do not pre-fatigue.
blocks.standard: The final warm-up is technically clean, below RPE 6 and leaves the athlete ready for the first work set.

blocks.name: Competition squat - top single
blocks.instruction: 1 x 1 @ RPE 6.5
blocks.standard: Every repetition meets the chosen competition standard or the clearly stated variation standard. Stop before a miss or technical breakdown.
blocks.rest: 3-5 minutes; longer before a heavy single when genuinely needed

blocks.name: Competition squat - back-off work
blocks.instruction: 4 x 5 @ 70%; cap RPE 7
blocks.standard: Every repetition meets the chosen competition standard or the clearly stated variation standard. Stop before a miss or technical breakdown.
blocks.rest: 3-5 minutes; longer before a heavy single when genuinely needed

blocks.name: Competition bench - volume
blocks.instruction: 4 x 5 @ 67.5%; cap RPE 7
blocks.standard: Every repetition meets the chosen competition standard or the clearly stated variation standard. Stop before a miss or technical breakdown.
blocks.rest: 3-5 minutes; longer before a heavy single when genuinely needed

blocks.name: Accessory capacity
blocks.instruction: Complete in order. Split squat or leg press - 3 x 8-10 @ 2-3 RIR | Leg curl - 3 x 10-12 @ 2 RIR | Weighted plank - 3 x 30-45 seconds
blocks.standard: Use controlled range and the stated RIR/RPE. No forced repetitions or failure.
blocks.rest: 90-180 seconds

blocks.name: Review and downshift
blocks.instruction: Walk or cycle easily for 3-5 minutes if useful. Record exact work, readiness, pain, first technical limiter and the next decision.
blocks.standard: Leave with a written record and no unreported changes.

blocks.standard: Every repetition meets the chosen competition standard or the clearly stated variation standard. Stop before a miss or technical breakdown.
blocks.rest: 3-5 minutes; longer before a heavy single when genuinely needed

blocks.name: Accessory capacity
blocks.instruction: No accessory work. Finish the session, eat, hydrate and recover.
blocks.standard: Use controlled range and the stated RIR/RPE. No forced repetitions or failure.
blocks.rest: 90-180 seconds

blocks.name: Review and downshift
blocks.instruction: Walk or cycle easily for 3-5 minutes if useful. Record exact work, readiness, pain, first technical limiter and the next decision.
blocks.standard: Leave with a written record and no unreported changes.

sessions.coach_note: Secondary work serves the competition lifts. Do not turn variations into ego lifts.

sessions.title: Competition or controlled total test
sessions.purpose: Express the best valid total available today without forcing a predetermined number.
sessions.intensity: Primers RPE 6 or lower; testing/competition follows attempt plan.
sessions.readiness_adjustment: Complete the readiness check before training. Percentage loads never override the RPE cap, movement standard or pain rule.

blocks.name: General and specific warm-up
blocks.instruction: 5-8 minutes easy movement, then 2-4 mobility or activation drills that improve today's competition platform lifts. Build through empty-bar and progressively heavier sets using low repetitions. Warm up; do not pre-fatigue.
blocks.standard: The final warm-up is technically clean, below RPE 6 and leaves the athlete ready for the first work set.

blocks.name: Select the Week 8 path
blocks.instruction: Competition: follow the event and federation. Gym test: simulate three attempts per lift with safeties, spotters and full standards. Training peak: take one single per lift up to RPE 8 and stop.
blocks.standard: The athlete selects one path before warming up. No spontaneous weight cut, fourth attempt or repeated miss.

blocks.name: Squat, bench press and deadlift attempts
blocks.instruction: Use the saved attempt plan. Complete squat, then bench press, then deadlift. For a gym test, take up to three attempts per lift and allow full recovery. Stop a lift after pain, unsafe equipment, repeated technical failure or a missed second attempt without a clear safe reason to continue.
blocks.standard: Only valid competition-standard lifts count toward the total.

blocks.name: Review and downshift
blocks.instruction: Walk or cycle easily for 3-5 minutes if useful. Record exact work, readiness, pain, first technical limiter and the next decision.
blocks.standard: Leave with a written record and no unreported changes.

sessions.coach_note: A total requires valid lifts. The day is not rescued by unsafe attempts.

sessions.title: Optional recovery + education
sessions.purpose: Improve recovery and turn programme education into one practical decision.
sessions.readiness_adjustment: Complete the readiness check before training. Percentage loads never override the RPE cap, movement standard or pain rule.

blocks.name: Easy recovery
blocks.instruction: 20-30 minutes easy walk, cycle, row or swim at conversational effort. Reduce to 10-20 minutes or complete relaxed mobility only when tired.
blocks.standard: Finish feeling better than you started. This is not conditioning and is genuinely optional.

blocks.name: After Week 8
blocks.instruction: A peak is followed by recovery and review, not an immediate second peak. Take several days away from heavy lifting after a maximal test or competition. Review successful lifts, failed standards, readiness, pain and bodyweight context. Update reference maxes only from valid results. Choose one technical and one physical priority for the next block. Return to accumulation before another peak unless the next event demands a carefully coached exception.
blocks.standard: Record one decision that changes training, recovery or meet preparation.

sessions.coach_note: Skip this session when complete rest better supports the following week.
